newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Daily Variety - April 17.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Daily Variety - April 17.

text.p: The following stories appeared in Thursday's Daily Variety:
* Better-than-expected growth in cable programming and cable systems helped Time Warner shrink its net loss and post a 17 percent increase in earnings before taxes, interest and other charges.
* Grupo Televisa founding chairman Emilio Azcarraga Milmo, Latin America's pre-eminent media mogul, died Wednesday at the age of 66.

* A day after the Los Angeles Times reported that owners of home-based businesses had until June 5 to register with the city and pay three years in back business taxes, the city has revised its position to extend the amnesty deadline until Sept. 5 and to waive all back taxes.

* European Union television viewers will have free access to major sports and cultural events due to an agreement between representatives of the European Parliament and European Union culture ministers.

* Walt Disney Interactive is the latest company to suffer casualties as the entertainment CD-ROM business continues its free-fall. A Disney Interactive spokeswoman confirmed the company has laid off 90 of its 425 staffers.
* After a late Tuesday evening meeting, the movie "Apaches" was sold to Disney's Touchstone and producer Jerry Bruckheimer.
